  "text": "In the morning Tobias took the church road home. He had sat all night in the last pew, with his cap between his knees. When the woman came to sweep, he lifted his feet for her.

There was wind now. At Maren’s gate it carried the smell of wet rope from the beach.

He counted the posts without meaning to. Eleven. The last stood beside the porch, its top worn pale where her father used to rest his hand.

The door was shut.

Tobias knocked, then waited with his knuckles against the wood. He had brought nothing. All the way from the church he had been thinking he ought to bring something, bread or milk, as though she had been ill.

Through the front window he could see the lamp on the sill. Unlit. Beyond it were the chair, the cold grate, the rug with one corner folded under.

He went round to the kitchen. Yesterday’s cup stood upside down on the draining board. Her coat hung from its peg.

He came back to the porch and straightened the mat with his boot.

At noon he told the woman from the church that Maren was not at home. She asked whether he had tried the door.

He looked at his hand.

That evening he returned with a loaf wrapped in paper. He left it on the step, clear of the rain, and knocked once before he remembered.

Inside, very quietly, a chair was drawn across the floor.

He waited until it stopped.",
